profiles.meeting_scenario: The search tooling team is holding a troubleshooting meeting after their internal Rebug-Detector prototype behaved inconsistently on a Lucene-Java validation batch. In the latest run, the tool flagged 87 candidate related bugs around a recently fixed Analyzer regression, but code reviewers said many flagged methods were irrelevant while a few overloads and one overridden variant that maintainers expected to see were absent from the review queue. The meeting happens the afternoon before a demo to the platform architecture group. The agenda is to diagnose whether the inconsistency comes from how bug text is extracted from JIRA issues, how an issue is anchored to a specific bug method in code, how cached stages were reused during reruns, or how the team is judging whether the detector 'caught' the related methods at all. The expected outcome is a shared troubleshooting plan for tonight's rerun and a concrete hypothesis about why the analyzer bug family was handled poorly.

members.name: Priya Natarajan
members.expertise: Java code indexing, call graph construction, issue-to-code linking, source analysis pipelines
members.background: Priya has spent six years building internal code intelligence systems and recently implemented the stage that maps Lucene issue artifacts to concrete methods and then expands across override and overload families for the detector.
members.private_state: Priya wants to protect confidence in the code-analysis portion of the prototype before tomorrow's demo and quietly hopes the problem can be framed as an input-quality or evaluation-setup issue rather than a flaw in the family-expansion design; she also wants to avoid a full pipeline rebuild because the raw issue export has been slow and brittle this week.
hidden_assumptions: When engineers say 'bug report text,' they normally mean the issue as stored at analysis time, including later clarifications, stack traces, and developer comments added before resolution.
The most defensible 'bug method' is the concrete implementation method that the fixing commit modified, because that is the closest auditable locus of the defect.

If one method in an overload or override family is actually edited to fix the bug, related-bug search should radiate outward from that edited method rather than from the API entry point that merely exposed the symptom.
A 'clean rerun' in this pipeline means invalidating derived analysis artifacts that depend on code features and rankings, not necessarily re-ingesting stable upstream issue data.
If a missed related method appears above the detector's suspicion threshold anywhere in the result set, the system has technically caught it even if reviewers would not notice it immediately.

members.name: Ethan Morales
members.expertise: bug triage workflows, defect validation, issue repository mining, reviewer evaluation protocols
members.background: Ethan previously maintained triage automation for Apache-style projects and now owns validation for whether the detector's outputs match how maintainers would actually reason from a reported Lucene bug to nearby risky methods.
members.private_state: Ethan wants tomorrow's output to be credible to human reviewers rather than merely defensible in pipeline terms, and he quietly suspects the prototype is benefiting from post-fix information that would not have been available when the bug was first reported; he also needs the next run to remain comparable with the spreadsheet used in earlier validation rounds.
hidden_assumptions: When evaluators say 'bug report text,' they usually mean the report as available near filing time: the description, reproduction notes, and early clarifications before fix discussion adds hindsight.
The practical 'bug method' is the method implicated by the externally visible symptom, because that is where reviewers begin checking sibling overloads and overrides.
For this detector, family expansion should start from the API-facing method named or implied by the report, even if the eventual patch touches a helper lower in the stack.
A 'clean rerun' should rebuild from raw issue export through method linking and ranking so the outputs are comparable to prior validation and unaffected by stale parsing assumptions.
The detector has only really caught a related method if it lands high enough in the reviewable slice that a maintainer would inspect, not merely somewhere in the full ranked output.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the bug report text
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about 'using the bug report text' to extract bug features for the analyzer issue.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the full JIRA issue thread as available now for LUCENE-7421, including later comments where a developer mentions token reuse behavior and names the helper method eventually patched.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means only the original description and early reproduction comments from the first day or two of LUCENE-7421, before patch discussion introduced solution-specific language.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In issue-mining discussions, 'bug report text' sounds like a mundane, already-settled artifact, and both are accustomed to teammates informally treating the issue as a single document rather than a time-sliced record, so the boundary difference hides inside a familiar phrase.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the bug method
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to anchoring the search on 'the bug method' for the analyzer regression.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the concrete implementation method changed by the fix commit, such as the internal reusableTokenStream helper actually edited in the patch.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the API-level analyzer method whose behavior users reported as failing, such as the public tokenStream or reusableTokenStream entry point from which a maintainer would inspect sibling overloads and overrides.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use singular language as though each issue naturally has one obvious method, and in many simpler bugs the symptom-level method and patch-level method coincide, so neither expects the other to be grounding 'bug method' at a different layer of the call stack.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to do 'a clean rerun tonight' before checking tomorrow's outputs.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to keep the existing parsed issue cache and bug-method links, then rebuild only the family-expansion, code-feature extraction, and similarity-ranking stages so the run finishes overnight.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the team to discard the current issue parse for LUCENE-7421 and rerun from raw JIRA export through feature extraction, method linking, and ranking so the analyzer case is re-evaluated end to end.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Within engineering teams, 'clean rerun' is a routine reassurance phrase rather than a formally specified operation, and each person's notion of what must be cleared follows naturally from the failure stage they privately suspect, making the divergence feel too obvious to articulate.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to catch the missing family members
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the next run should 'catch the missing overloads' from the analyzer bug family.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the detector has caught them if those overloads and the overridden variant clear the global suspiciousness cutoff and appear anywhere in the candidate list for that issue, even if they rank around positions 18-25.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the detector has caught them only if they appear in the top review slice a maintainer would realistically inspect, roughly the first 10 candidates shown in the validation spreadsheet.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'catch the missing overloads' sounds operationally shared and is common shorthand in troubleshooting conversations, but one person is silently applying a system-level threshold notion while the other is applying a human-review visibility standard, and neither hears the phrase as requiring formal clarification.

Also, a full raw issue reingest tonight would be painful with the export pipeline unstable.
